source: NCERT Class XII, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 2), Ch. 5 (The Pahari Schools of Painting).

sections.heading: 1. Pahari Painting — Overview
points: **Pahari painting** developed in the **hill states of the Himalayan foothills** (Himachal Pradesh, Jammu region) in the 17th–19th centuries ('pahari' = of the hills).
Themes: mostly **Vaishnava devotion** — **Krishna-lila, Gita Govinda, Bhagavata Purana, Ragamala, Barahmasa, Nayaka-Nayika**.
Two main schools: **Basohli** and **Kangra**.

sections.heading: 2. The Basohli School
points: **Basohli (Jammu region)** — the **earliest** Pahari school (17th c.).
Style: **bold, intense colours (bright red, yellow), strong lines, large expressive eyes**, and the use of **beetle-wing cases for jewellery** (shining green).
Famous work: the **Rasamanjari** series (poetry on love/heroes-heroines).

sections.heading: 3. The Kangra School
points: **Kangra (Himachal Pradesh)** — the most refined Pahari school (late 18th c.), flourished under **Raja Sansar Chand**.
Grew from the **Guler** style (naturalism from migrating Mughal-trained artists — **Nainsukh, Manaku**).
Style: **delicate, lyrical, soft colours, graceful female figures, tender romantic mood** — especially the **Gita Govinda** and Krishna-Radha themes.
The Kangra style is regarded as the **finest of the Pahari schools**.

sections.heading: 4. Other Centres and Significance
points: Other centres: **Guler, Chamba, Garhwal, Mandi, Kullu, Nurpur**.
Pahari painting is deeply **devotional and poetic**, celebrating love and nature.
It represents the last great phase of Indian miniature painting.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Pahari = Himalayan hill states; themes = Krishna-lila, Gita Govinda, Ragamala.
Basohli = earliest Pahari school; bold intense colours; beetle-wing jewellery; Rasamanjari.
Kangra = finest Pahari school; Raja Sansar Chand; delicate, lyrical; from Guler style.
Artists: Nainsukh, Manaku (Guler-Kangra).
Other centres: Guler, Chamba, Garhwal, Mandi.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Basohli = earliest Pahari school** (bold colours, beetle-wing jewellery).
**Kangra = finest/most refined** Pahari school (Raja Sansar Chand; delicate, lyrical).
**Nainsukh** was a famous Pahari (Guler) painter.
Pahari themes are largely **Vaishnava/Krishna** devotional.
